items.title: No account of burden from residents, assessors and administrators together
items.whyItMatters: Only nine reports asked both residents and assessors, and none added administrators (c4); the committee needs all three perspectives before changing targets.
items.opportunity: Sample all three groups in one study and compare accounts by role.

items.title: Why assessments are late is unknown
items.whyItMatters: Log data show delay and thin comments (c2) but cannot explain them; the local export repeats the pattern.
items.opportunity: Ask assessors directly about the conditions of late completion and use the export only to describe the setting.

items.title: Struggling residents may be missing from the evidence
items.whyItMatters: Residents who struggle request the fewest assessments and may also decline interviews, so their experience would be silently absent.
items.opportunity: Invite residents with low assessment counts through a neutral channel and report whether they took part.

items.title: Interviewer power over participants
items.whyItMatters: Residents may not speak freely to anyone involved in progression decisions.
items.opportunity: Interviews by the research assistant, de-identified transcripts before the programme director reads them.

items.title: Effect of changing the target is untested
items.whyItMatters: The only report of a lower target is uncontrolled (c3); the interviews cannot show an effect.
items.opportunity: Record participants' views on target changes as proposals for the committee, not as findings about effect.

errorsFound: The need's phrase 'burden' covers time, cognitive, emotional and administrative load; the study must say which it examines rather than treat them as one.
reevaluation: The gaps confirm a qualitative study across three roles, with care for who is missing and who asks the questions.
summary: Five gaps; missing multi-role accounts and unexplained delay are high severity.
